where: Stage 1 Sketch. topics.js drawSketch (lines 390-414) and schedule (253-264). review-shots/sheet-A-start.png, plus a per-frame log of a real play at 1370x860.
problem: Play opens by dissolving the finished drawing to a 30% ghost (t -0.42 to -0.10, pencil lying still), then redraws it: the first motion is the drawing disappearing. The pencil then jumps 294 px in one frame at t=0.009 and chases 414 strokes in 2.05 s: 8,641 px of travel on a 924 px sheet, 68 of 123 frames move more than 40 px, the worst 303 px. The follow factor (.42 per frame, line 411) also runs twice as fast on a 120 Hz screen.
change: 1) Delete the erase (fo, lines 394 and 403). At rest show the structure firm (frame, dividers, boxes, word scribbles) and hold back only the parts made by num() and hatch() (flag them late in add()); their 30% underdrawing stays. 2) Play draws only the late parts: the 4 KPI numbers left to right 0-0.45 s, then the 5 tiles darkest first (g.order, the same order stage 3 uses), hatch then score, 0.16 s apart, 0.45-1.25 s. D1 = 1.3, so stage 1 drops from 2.15 s to 1.4 s. 3) Pickup: over t -0.42 to 0 move the pencil from its resting place to the first stroke's start with ioC, rotating -5deg to -52deg. 4) Follow by time, not by frame: 1 - Math.exp(-dt*16) for x and y, 1 - Math.exp(-dt*8) for rotation, tip speed capped at 1400 px/s.
better_change: Parts 3 (pickup over t -0.42..0) and 4 (time-based follow, 1 - exp(-dt*16)) are safe and should be done as written. Parts 1-2 are a redesign that changes the resting frame the owner sees first (numbers and hatching drop to the 30% underdrawing), so they need his eye, and as written they conflict with themselves: (a) 'flag the parts made by num() and hatch() late' also catches the six list-row scores (num(5,...), line 234), which get no slot in the proposed 0-1.25 s schedule and would stay ghosted until the wireframe takes them; flag only groups 3 and 4. (b) Darkest-first tile order (g.order = k 4,0,3,1,2) makes the pencil cross the map on every tile, about 200-245 window px per hop every 0.16 s, plus dozens of hatch lines per tile; the proposed 1400 px/s cap cannot cover that, so strokes will appear ahead of the tip. Give the pencil one anchor per tile (its score number) and one sweep along the KPI row, let the hatch fill in under it, and order tiles by nearest neighbour in stage 1 (stage 3 can keep darkest-first). If the owner wants the whole sheet drawn live as now, keep the erase but still apply parts 3-4 and the one-anchor-per-region rule; that alone removes the 296 px first-frame jump and most of the 8,700 px.

better_change: One part of the change breaks on wider screens: the front cloud 'drifts in from beyond the right edge, translateX 300, no fade'. The cloud's left edge is (vw - 1160)/2 + 988 px, so +300 is outside the viewport only up to about 1416 px wide. Use a start offset computed in buildWorld (vw - cloud left + 20) or keep a 120 ms opacity ramp. The rest (city revealed bottom-up by a mask instead of opacity, hydrangeas and wisteria with a 120 ms ramp, wisteria from u 1.0, delete the invisible sky drift, cloud drift 20 px) is sound and touches nothing in the window's registration; I could not render it, being read-only. change: One gesture for the whole body, the same left-to-right wipe the list rows already use: replace line 314 with sh.wipe(tl.r, ioS(seg(t, h.tile + .14*j, h.tile + .14*j + .32)), 24) in g.order (darkest first); delete the region radial on line 315 and wipe only the map's header strip (bodyTop to first tile top) at h.tile and its legend (last tile bottom to H) at h.tile + .6, each .4 s. For the vanishing controls add to LO_MATCH '.lofi .tp-h .tp-n,.lofi .tp-h .tp-seg{display:none!important}', or include them in the planned product fix, so nothing is lost between stage 2 and 3.
better_change: Two corrections. 1) Deleting the region radial and wiping only tile rects plus a header strip and a legend strip leaves holes in the mask. Measured on the live page: the map region R.map starts at x 217.7 (the sidebar's edge) but the tiles start at x 272.9 and end at 864.5 against the split at 877.8. The 55 px strip left of the tiles holds the card's own left edge and padding, which differ between the wireframe and the finished page; it would stay wireframe until hiDone (5.81) and then pop in one frame. Extend each tile's wipe rect to the region's edge when the tile touches the map's edge (x -> g.R.map.x for the left column, r -> g.R.map.r for the right), and update line 274 to .14*(n-1)+.32. 2) Do not add '.lofi .tp-h .tp-n,.lofi .tp-h .tp-seg{display:none}' to LO_MATCH. The numbered notes are the wireframe's annotations, the page's rules say the low-fidelity wireframe stays as it is, and the rule would hide notes 2 and 4 while notes 1 and 3 (in .tp-def and .key) stay. Notes leaving at stage 3 is the right story. The segmented controls are hidden by the product itself ('.stage:not(.lofi) .tp-h .tp-seg{display:none}', product topics.css line 267); that is the same wireframe-against-finished difference already accepted and waiting for the planned product fix, so it is not a finding for this block.

where: The sentence under the steps, all stages. topics.js drawSteps lines 444-448; index.html .tp-say. Contact strip shots/10-contact-strip.png.
problem: A new 8 to 10 word sentence in 16 px gray appears every 1.6 to 2.1 s, about 200 px above the action; stage 2's nine words are fully visible for 1.21 s (1.59 minus .28 fade-in and .10 fade-out), so the visitor either reads or watches. The last swap is a cut: caption 5 comes in over 10 ms (seg(t, T-.01, T)) and caption 4 has no fade-out because of the j < 4 test.
change: During the full play show no sentence after stage 1: fade says[0] out at B[1]-.1 and keep says[1..4] at 0; the five step names and the filling line already say where the play is. Show a stage's sentence only when its step was pressed and held (set a solo flag in the step button's playRange call). End: caption 4 out over T-.45 to T-.3, caption 5 in over 300 ms, seg(t, T-.3, T), timed to the answer landing. If the owner wants words during the play, they must be 4 words or fewer per stage.
better_change: The end swap fix is right as written. For the middle, the proposal's own second option is the safer one: silence drops the two facts no picture can carry ('on the same code', 'one real question'), so keep a sentence per stage but cut each to four words or fewer; the wording is the owner's. If the sentences are instead shown only for a pressed step, keep the aria-describedby targets in the DOM (they are, the change only sets opacity).

where: Outside the play: the replay button, the step buttons, reduced motion. topics.js playRange line 492, again handler 494, step click 509, calm lines 19 and 517; topics.css lines 38-39.
problem: Replay and step 1 set time to REST and render in the same frame, so the painted sky, city, flowers, blue window and open Ask panel are replaced by the pale sheet in one frame. Under reduced motion the block correctly lands on the end state, but every step button and the replay button still run the full motion (playRange has no calm branch): 2 s of pencil and 1.5 s of brush. The .is-dip rule made for this exists in the CSS and is never used.
change: Replay or any backward jump from t > B[1]: fade .tp-fig to opacity 0 over 180 ms, then set time and render(true), fade back over 220 ms, then start the clock. Under calm: a step button does the same dip and then seek(i < 4 ? B[i+1] : T) with no playback, and .tp-again is hidden. Either use .is-dip for this or delete lines 38-39.
better_change: The dip is right, but its timing must cover one more thing the finding missed: after a played stage 5, useReset (line 358) schedules a remeasure that rebuilds the whole pencil drawing (buildSketch empties the SVG) and snaps the pencil. In my log of a replay the sketch was rebuilt 538 ms and 954 ms after the click, at play time 0.03 and 0.47, in the middle of the drawing. So when the Ask panel was open, hold the figure dipped for about 520 ms (420 + 90, lines 358 and 83) before fading back and starting the clock, and cancel the second remeasure (mT2) once playing, or skip buildSketch while `playing`. The 180 ms + 220 ms dip as proposed would start the clock before the first rebuild. Also fade only the stage and world layers, not the whole .tp-fig, if the step row should stay steady (the steps are outside .tp-fig, so either works).

where: Stages 4-5 and final. Shots 05, 07, 08 against the left half of 11. art/sky.webp, art/city.webp, .tp-sky-img, .a-city (topics.css line 55)
problem: The sky is a near-uniform cobalt slab where the chosen sketch is airy. Measured outside the window, the average blue pixel is (84,157,221) in shot 07 against (118,187,236) in the sketch; open sky is about (48,147,234) against (158,205,246). The plate is only about 6% cloud, where the sketch lets cloud carry most of the sky and pales toward the bottom and the page edge. The city's glass (12,96,174) is the darkest, most saturated thing in the frame and pulls the eye to the left margin; the sketch's towers sit near (63,165,228) in haze.
change: Today, as proof: .tp-sky-img{opacity:.72} and .a-city{filter:saturate(.72) brightness(1.1) contrast(.9)}. For the repaint (the art is marked DRAFT; a new plate needs the owner's eye on a cheap draft first): key the sky at about #76BBEC on average, clouds over at least 25% of the plate, deepest blue only at the top right behind the wisteria, palest along the bottom and wherever the sky meets the page, and a city painted in aerial haze no darker than #3FA5E4.

where: Stages 4-5 and final. Shots 05, 07, 08, strip-end. topics.js line 328 (BR) and lines 329-345 (buildWorld), line 427 (sky drift), line 430 (parallax)
problem: The sky's upper boundary is the straight side of a single stroke (BR[3], v=-225, u -760 to 900): one ruler line at about -19 degrees from (0,440) to (980,95) in shot 07, with an even 25px airbrushed feather, so it reads as a blue wedge; in the sketch that border wanders through clouds. Separately, every played frame (07, 08, strip-end, x-live-real-hover) has a 3-4px bare strip with a hard vertical cut at the left viewport edge (x=0-2 is #f4f3f1 at y=500, 600, 750), because the sky is exactly viewport-wide while it drifts 5px and parallaxes 6px.
change: 1) In buildWorld draw each stroke as a bowed path, not M..L: 'M u1,v Q (u1+u2)/2,v+bow u2,v' with bow = [-34,22,-18,40,-26,30,-14,20]*k, and start BR[3] at u=-560 instead of -760 so no neighbouring strokes share one edge. 2) Put a painted cloud on the hardest stretch of the edge: cut the plate's top-centre cloud with cut-art.py as cloud-back.webp, place it in .tp-mid at left:calc(var(--L) + var(--sw)*.62); top:-150px; width:300px, so it shows from behind the wisteria's left side, clear of step 5 (ends x=795) and the heading (ends x=810). 3) Bleed the sky past the viewport: .tp-far{left:calc(50% - 50vw - 16px); width:calc(100vw + 32px)} and add 16 to cx in buildWorld.
better_change: 1) The bow is too small to see: a quadratic's midpoint moves only half the control offset, so 7 to 20px over a 1,600px stroke. Use at least three times the values, or rely on the cloud. 2) The cloud cut is free (cut-art.py is local PIL); I did not test it. 3) Do not widen .tp-far and add 16 to cx: the SVG has preserveAspectRatio=none and a viewBox of vw, so that stretches the sky 2.3% and moves the strokes about 17px right at the window centre and 33px at the right edge. Instead, in buildWorld: skyImg x=-16, width=vw+32; mask x=-16, width=vw+32; start the strokes that begin at u<-700 60 further left. Tested (review-shots/sk2-edge-alt.png): 0 bare pixels on both sides, geometry unchanged.

where: All window stages, worst in the final live state. Shots 07, 06, 00. topics.css line 25 (--stw) and line 26; topics.js line 73 (fit)
problem: The window's inner width is 904px, so the 1440px product page is drawn at 0.63: 12px product text shows at 7.6px and 11px at 6.9px. The block on the page today (shot 00) draws the same page at about 0.79. The payoff suffers most: the Ask AI panel is about 184px wide, 'Ask AI' wraps onto two lines, its title is cut to 'Satisfaction on Changes & Canc...', and the answer is set in 7.6px type.
change: First, at no cost in height: in fit() try [1280,720,''] for the desktop tier instead of [1440,810,''], which gives a scale of 0.71; check the Ask-open state in studio.html at 1280 before keeping it (I did not run it). Second, on viewports at least 860px tall: @media (min-height:860px){.tp-fig{--stw:min(90%,1040px)} .ct-stage{margin-left:calc((100% - var(--stw))/2 + 30px)} .a-city{left:calc(var(--L) - 205px); width:280px} .a-wisteria{top:-220px}}. Both together reach 0.80, the legibility of today's block.
better_change: Drop the 1280 change; it does nothing. The wider window only fits from about 940px of viewport height (stage bottom 898, more under the site header), so gate it at min-height:940px or first take about 60px out of the head. A lever that costs no height: draw the pages below the product's zoom floor of 0.72 (1,238px). I ran fit() at [1100, 619, ''] (review-shots/sk2-fit1100-play.png): text about 13% larger in the same 924px window, layout classes unchanged, everything fits. But the scripted Ask did not open in that run (no ask-on at the end) and one list label truncated to 'Changes & Cancell...', so it needs work before use. The 'Ask AI' wrap is a 37px-wide <b> in the product's own panel header: fix it there (white-space:nowrap), not by scale.

where: Stage 1 and the resting frame. Shots 01, 02, 09-390-rest. topics.js lines 145-150 (zig), 165-168 and 213 (hatch), 129 (stroke weight); topics.css lines 28 and 44; index.html line 28 (caption)
problem: It reads as a wireframe put through a sketch filter, not graphite. Every line of words is the same periodic sawtooth, like a spell-check underline; the hatching is exact 45-degree lines that all stop precisely on the box edge (over:0), and the darkest tile is two passes in the same direction; no stroke changes pressure along its length. The caption says 'on the page itself' while the drawing sits on a separate card with a 1px ring and a drop shadow, and the drawn frame hugs that card 15px in on all four sides like a printed border.
change: zig(): replace the sawtooth with broken straight runs: word runs of 14-44px with 5-8px gaps, each drawn with ln() at amp .5; titles get two passes 1px apart. hatch(): per-end overshoot random between -2 and +4px, angle jitter of plus or minus 4 degrees, and make the dark tile's second pass cross at -30 degrees instead of repeating 45. Pressure: stroke #3b3c41 instead of #27282b, and split any line over 120px into two paths with the second at 65% opacity. Paper: commit to the caption: .tp-sheet{background:var(--tooth); box-shadow:none; -webkit-mask:radial-gradient(closest-side,#000 82%,transparent); mask:radial-gradient(closest-side,#000 82%,transparent)} so the drawn frame is the only rectangle.
better_change: The stroke changes are sound. Two notes on the paper. The radial mask adds nothing: closest-side on a 924x527 box is an ellipse, and the tooth is too faint to see either way, so just use .tp-sheet{background:none; box-shadow:none}. And removing the sheet is the owner's call: he asked for 'a sketch on paper', and the CSS comment calls the sheet 'the sheet that becomes the window'. The cheaper way to end the mismatch is the caption: 'It starts in pencil, on paper.'

where: Stage 4 onward. Shots 05, 07 against the sketch in 11. topics.css lines 32, 33, 59; topics.js line 424; art/cloud-front.webp
problem: Nothing sits in front of the window on the right, so it is pasted on the sky. The front cloud's mass is on the right of its cut-out and lands at x 1208-1418, 11px outside the window's right edge (1197), where the sketch's cloud clearly covers the bottom-right corner. The sun glint is a 32%-wide pale yellow tint (about #FFE6B0) that reads as a stain on the white bezel. A hairline arc shows inside the bezel at every corner in shots 03, 04 and 07, where the two box-shadows of .ct-stage::after fail to meet.
change: Cloud: mirror it (add ' scaleX(-1)' to the extra argument of put(art.front, ...)) and set .a-cloud-front{left:calc(var(--L) + var(--sw) - 170px); top:calc(var(--sh) - 30px); width:400px}, so its top crosses only the bottom 20px of bezel and page margin, never the Ask input or the list. Erase the stray streak at about (30-95, 110-145) in cloud-front.webp. Glint: .tp-sun{left:8%; width:14%; height:3px} with a 12px round bloom at its left end, or delete it. Bezel: .ct-stage::after{inset:8px; border:6px solid #fff; border-radius:16px; box-shadow:none}.
better_change: Keep the change, with two additions. 1) The moved cloud's box ends at y=943 while the block ends at 897, so about 30px of visible cloud hangs into whatever follows on the real page: add .tp-block{padding-bottom:110px} at 900px and wider, or cut the width to 340px. 2) The rule at max-width:700px (topics.css 105) re-declares inset:5px and both box-shadows; with the new 6px border the phone bezel would cover 6px of content, not 2.5px. Change it to .ct-stage::after{inset:3px; border-width:4.5px; border-radius:13px; box-shadow:none}.

where: Head, every stage. Shots 01, 07, 13-1370x770-final, 00. index.html lines 17-34; topics.css lines 64-84; topics.js line 545
problem: The head has three left edges: label and heading at x=105, steps and caption at x=165 behind a 44px white replay disc that holds the heading's own edge, and the final caption at x=183 after its blue dot. The equal 118px columns leave gaps of 63, 30, 48 and 15px between labels, so '5 In use' is jammed against '4 Hear's world'. At the end, five ink bars sit under the heading as a second heavy rule. From label to window bottom the block needs 750px; under the site's roughly 60px header (shot 00) at 1370x770, the bottom of the window, where all of stage 5 plays (tooltip at y 700-818 in shot 06), is below the fold.
change: Move .tp-again after .tp-steps and make it quiet: width and height 32px, background none, box-shadow none, color #6b7077. .tp-say{margin-left:0}; .tp-dot{position:absolute; margin-left:-18px}. .tp-steps li{width:134px} and .tp-head{max-width:800px}. .tp-steps li.done .tp-line i{background:#9aa0a6}. Tighten: .tp-head .label{margin-bottom:12px}; .tp-bar{margin-top:16px}; .tp-fig{margin-top:24px}. Start the play at threshold .85 instead of .5 so the bottom of the window is on screen when stage 5 runs.
better_change: Mostly right; three corrections. 1) The tightening saves 22px (stage 284..811), so the block still needs 726px against 710 available at 770: say so, do not claim it fits. 2) Threshold .85 still lets the bottom 79px of the window be off screen, and the asked tile sits in the bottom quarter. Compute it: threshold = Math.min(.98, (innerHeight - headerHeight - 16) / stage.offsetHeight). 3) The hanging dot lands at x=87 on desktop, fine as a hanging bullet, but on a phone (24px padding) it sits 6px from the screen edge with its halo at 2px: keep the dot inline under 900px.

where: Rest and stage 1. Shots 01, 02, 09-390-rest, 13-1370x770-rest. index.html lines 68-74; topics.css line 45; topics.js lines 407 and 413
problem: The pencil is a stock flat icon beside impasto paintings: three flat yellow bands, a plain triangle tip, a 170px body at about 11:1 where a real pencil is near 25:1, and one even drop shadow although the tip touches the paper and the eraser end is raised. At rest it straddles the sheet's bottom edge, half on and half off, which looks like a mistake, and at 1370x770 it is under the fold, so the resting frame has no pencil at all.
change: Redraw in SVG at viewBox 0 0 260 12: a hexagonal body in three facets (narrow highlight #ffe07a, core #f3bd34, shade #c98f14), a scalloped paint line of three arcs where the wood begins, a wood cone with a darker lower third, a graphite tip with a 1px highlight, a ferrule with two crimp rings and a light band, an eraser with a top highlight. Replace the drop-shadow filter with a separate shadow path that meets the tip and stands 7px off at the eraser. Rest position: tx = ox + w + 52, ty = oy + h*.72, tr = -64 (in the right margin, where the sky later arrives); fall back to today's position when less than 130px is free to the right of the window. If a painted pencil is wanted instead, that is a paid cut-out and needs the owner's eye on a draft.
better_change: The fallback threshold is wrong. At -64 degrees a 260px pencil reaches about 165px right of the window; at 1370 its box is x=1232..1358, 12px from the viewport edge, and at about 1330 wide (153px free, which passes the 130 test) it is clipped by .tp-page{overflow:clip}. Use the margin position only when at least 190px is free to the right of the window, or stand it steeper (tr=-76, tx = ox + w + 44), which needs about 110px. A classic 15px scrollbar eats into the same margin.

where: 390px wide, stages 4-5. Shot 09-390-final. topics.css lines 86-101 (line 91 hides .tp-mid and .tp-near); topics.js lines 332 and 341
problem: On a phone step 4, 'Hear's world', shows two blue tabs about 12px wide sticking out left and right of the window between y 500 and 680, with no cloud, flower or city. They read as a rendering fault, and the caption 'Hear's painted world is brushed in around it' has nothing to point at.
change: At max-width:899px give the world a band under the window: .tp-near{display:block} .a-wisteria{display:none} .a-hyd{left:-14px; top:calc(var(--sh) - 58px); width:150px} .a-cloud-front{left:calc(100vw - 230px); top:calc(var(--sh) - 22px); width:250px} .tp-block{padding-bottom:96px} .tp-sky{height:calc(var(--sh) + 230px)}. In buildWorld's small branch use hgt = sh + 230 and add one stroke below the window, [430,-500,900,120], and drop the strokes that only reach the side slivers (v between -230 and 200), so the sky appears as one painted band below, not as tabs at the sides.
better_change: In buildWorld's small branch: hgt = sh + 360; give the filter the whole sky (y=0, height=hgt); replace BR with two strokes set in screen pixels, [(sh/2 + 52)/k, -640, 900, 120/k] and [(sh/2 + 130)/k, -640, 900, 110/k]. CSS at max-width:899px: .tp-sky{height:calc(var(--sh) + 360px)} .tp-near{display:block} .a-wisteria{display:none} .a-hyd{left:-18px; top:calc(var(--sh) - 22px); width:130px} .a-cloud-front{left:calc(100vw - 215px); top:calc(var(--sh) + 6px); width:250px}. Tested (review-shots/sk2-phone-alt.png): one painted band under the window, flowers on the bezel corner only, legend clear. Still to tune: the band runs to the block's bottom edge at padding-bottom:150px, so use about 200px or lift the second stroke.
